gaps.note: MegaETH. The high-throughput unit cleared MegaETH on the statement that every arithmetic and jump instruction of mega-evm is the stock revm one, and on eth_call reruns. That covers the replica and RPC path only. MegaETH states that it uses just-in-time compilation to native code (https://www.megaeth.com/about, fetched 2026-11-24, section Bytecode Compilation), and megaeth-labs publishes an AOT compiler prototype that turns EVM bytecode into C++ that calls evmone opcode handlers on the intx library, with PUSH;JUMP and PUSH;JUMPI fused into super-instructions and per-block gas checks (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/megaeth-labs/evmone-compiler/master/README.md and lib/compiler/aot_compiler.hpp lines 10-98, fetched 2026-11-24). No cycle has asked which executor produces MegaETH blocks. The 5,833 and 39,074 mined swaps are the only evidence for that path, and they reach only the swap code at common values. This is the same blind spot that OPCODES.md records for Monad, with a different integer library (intx, not ruint) and no published source for the production build.

Monad. The cleared item of high-throughput for lead L-575 says the build has no MULMOD with a literal power of two modulus and that the battery therefore tests the code the blocks run. Its verifier found two such MULMODs (pc 22378 with modulus 2^128 from Position.sol:94 and 96 via FullMath.sol:48, and pc 22639 with modulus 2^96 from SqrtPriceMath.sol:240 and 250 via FullMath.sol:48) that compile to inline x86 through mul_mod2, mul_with_bit_size and MulEmitter, which no eth_call reaches and no mined swap has run. The clearance of L-575 is therefore incomplete for those two sites, and the MUL code generation that OPCODES.md lists as not read is still not read. The verifier's bound on the error rests on reading only.

Polygon, BNB Smart Chain, Avalanche. The arbitrum-family unit raised Go issue 81863 (a dead store pass that ignores a CondSelect of two local addresses and silently drops a store) for nitro built with go1.27.3. The same fault applies to the Go 1.26 line, which was fixed in go1.26.11 on 2026-11-10 (https://go.dev/doc/devel/release, fetched 2026-11-24; fix diff at https://go.googlesource.com/go/+/00ba484%5E%21/ adds OpCondSelect to the deadstore keep rule). Critic queries of web3_clientVersion on 2026-11-24 returned bor/ebcfea01452d and bor/280514fa9fb7 v2.11.1-private go1.26.10 (https://polygon-bor-rpc.publicnode.com), Geth/v1.8.2 go1.26.10 (https://bsc-dataseed1.bnbchain.org) and avalanchego/1.15.3 go=1.26.10 (https://api.avax.network/ext/bc/C/rpc). established-l1 did not consider the Go toolchain of these three clients. The battery passed on these very binaries, so only paths the vectors do not reach remain open.

Tempo, Arc, HyperEVM. These are three of the single-client networks that OPCODES.md asks to retest after every release, and none had a unit in cycle 9. Open since earlier cycles: the per-CPU jump destination scan of evm2 and the jit feature on Tempo validators (L-582, L-286); the commit behind arc/v1, which the Arc endpoint still reports on 2026-11-24; the closed HyperEVM validator (the endpoint reports only 'hyperliquid evm Mainnet'). Tempo still reports tempo/v1.19.0-697ea97, so the step trace comparison of OPCODES.md still applies to the endpoint build.

Ethereum and the OP Stack reth networks had no network unit in cycle 9. Lead L-583 can be partly settled: crates.io (https://crates.io/api/v1/crates/ruint/versions, fetched 2026-11-24) lists no ruint release after 1.21.1 of 2026-10-23, and 1.21.0 stays yanked. OP Mainnet answered with op-reth/v2.8.1-72207294 and twice with op-reth/v0.0.0-dev-unknown, so one backend of https://mainnet.optimism.io reports no version, and which ruint it links is not known.

Unichain. The 550 scripts still have never run the 24,050 byte genesis predeploy at 0x1f98400000000000000000000000000000000004 (L-584, L-426, L-092 open since cycle 8). The bytecode map of cycle 9 covers the build of this checkout only.

Elysium. Lead L-547 (transient rollback after a reverted unlock frame in a mined transaction) is answered for Robinhood Chain only. Elysium serves debug_traceTransaction only with an API key, and its node reports nitro/vlocal+unknown-unknown, so its build cannot be tied to a source tag.

MegaETH. The status of Rex6 stays unsettled: the Rex6 page says it is not scheduled on any network, while the mega-evm v1.7.3 changelog says it was scheduled on mainnet and testnet. The per call frame budgets of the resource limits spec (https://docs.megaeth.com/spec/megaevm/resource-limits.md, fetched 2026-11-24: each inner frame gets a fraction of its parent's remaining compute gas, data size, KV updates and state growth, and a frame that exceeds it reverts with MegaLimitExceeded) were never checked against the number of storage writes a PoolManager frame makes in a swap that crosses many ticks.

leads.question: Which executor produces MegaETH mainnet blocks for the PoolManager at 0xacb7e78fa05d562e0a5d3089ec896d57d057d38e: the mega-evm interpreter, the evmone-compiler AOT path of megaeth-labs/evmone-compiler, revmc, or another JIT? Ask the public docs, release notes and the stateless-validator source, and record whether the stateless validator re-executes blocks with the interpreter. If any compiled path is used, read lib/compiler/aot_compiler.hpp and compiler.cpp at master for PUSHnJUMPI (lines 86-98: does it test the whole 256 bit condition word, and does it keep the fall-through when the condition is zero), the compile-time is_jumpdest map against the 29 JUMPDEST bytes inside push data of this build, the per-block gas and stack checks, and the intx version that the evmone handlers for MULMOD, ADDMOD, SDIV, SMOD, SIGNEXTEND, SAR and BYTE link.
leads.why: Replica eth_call runs the interpreter, so 185,529 vectors and 550 scripts say nothing about the code that blocks run. A compiled JUMPI or MULMOD that differs from the specification would change a swap or liquidity amount in blocks only, for every pool, with an ordinary transaction as the trigger.

leads.question: If a compiled executor produces MegaETH blocks, find one mined transaction in which a frame that entered PoolManager.unlock reverted and a later frame of the same transaction completed an unlock, and one in which settle ran inside a reverted inner frame (on-chain quoters revert after a swap). Did the block producer roll back the transient unlock flag and the transient deltas of the reverted frame? Use debug_traceTransaction where any MegaETH endpoint serves it, otherwise the receipt and logs.
leads.why: src/libraries/CurrencyDelta.sol and src/libraries/Lock.sol keep the credit and the lock in transient storage, and src/PoolManager.sol:104-114 trusts the EVM to roll them back. A credit that survives a reverted payment frame lets any account take funds it never paid. Robinhood Chain answered this in cycle 9; MegaETH is the other network whose block path differs from its RPC path.

leads.question: Transcribe Monad v0.16.5 mul_mod2 for exp 96 and 128 and its call into mul_with_bit_size and MulEmitter (emitter.cpp lines 6381-6931 and 7990-8085) for two non-literal operands in each operand location, and compare mulmod(a, b, 2^96) and mulmod(a, b, 2^128) with the specification for a and b with all limbs set, low limbs zero, and both operands in one register. These are the MULMODs at pc 22378 (FullMath.sol:48 via Position.sol:94 and 96) and pc 22639 (FullMath.sol:48 via SqrtPriceMath.sol:240 and 250).
leads.why: Carried from the high-throughput verifier. No eth_call and no mined swap reaches these two compiled sites, and the bound that keeps a wrong remainder harmless rests on reading only.

leads.question: Transcribe the v0.16.5 x86 code generation for MUL with one literal operand (mul_optimized and its MulEmitter cases) and run it for the 19 multipliers of TickMath.getSqrtPriceAtTick (src/libraries/TickMath.sol:82-100), the first-step select at TickMath.sol:80, the signed multiply by 255738958999603826347141 at TickMath.sol:225, and mul(r, r) with the same operand at TickMath.sol:142-220, over every intermediate price the whole tick range produces. Then list which of the bits 0x20000, 0x40000 and 0x80000 of the absolute tick appear in the 17,434 Monad swaps of opcodes/swaps-deep.json and in the ticks of live positions.
leads.why: Any account can add liquidity at a tick it chooses, so getSqrtPriceAtTick runs in compiled code on an attacker chosen bit pattern, and the amounts owed for a position come from it (src/libraries/SqrtPriceMath.sol). A wrong price for a rarely used high bit would let a position be opened for less than it can later withdraw. Mined swaps rarely reach ticks above 2^17, and the whole-range test of cycle 9 ran in pyevm only.

leads.question: Under the per call frame budgets of https://docs.megaeth.com/spec/megaevm/resource-limits.md, how many initialized tick crossings can one swap make before the PoolManager frame, called from a router at depth 1 or 2, exceeds its KV-update or data-size share and reverts with MegaLimitExceeded? Measure with eth_call through a router on a pool with many dust ticks, and check whether modifyLiquidity to remove a position can hit the same limit.
leads.why: A frame budget that is a fraction of the parent's remaining budget does not scale with the gas the caller supplies. If an ordinary account can plant enough initialized ticks to push a victim's swap or removal over that share, it blocks the operation at no gas price, which is a freeze lever F-042, F-105 and F-111 did not test.

leads.question: Does holiman/uint256 (v1.3.2 for bor, bsc and nitro, v1.2.4 for libevm), core/vm or core/state of bor v2.11.1, bsc v1.8.2, libevm d398bc4dbe41 and the nitro go-ethereum fork 0e44603 contain the Go issue 81863 shape: a pointer chosen by a branch between the addresses of two local variables, followed by a store through it that a later read of one of the locals depends on? A store dropped on a path that the vectors do not reach would make those nodes compute another state than the specification, on chains whose block producers may run the same build.
